Moss could qualify the answer without claiming to have verified any hours. Asking whether Moss verified any hours gives counsel a basis for asking which ones.

Review excerpt: “If yes, identify the records and calculations”
Adjudicator reason: The affirmative answer establishes that Moss reviewed timecards. F4, p. 5, lines 1–8 identifies those records, and F3, p. 2, row B attributes the $6,400 to an estimate. Whether Moss used or reviewed calculations remains open. The proposed follow-up asks that question before requesting specifics.

Review excerpt: A qualified answer could concern Moss’s private understanding without establishing another **communicated** limitation.
Adjudicator reason: F1, p. 1, message 3 states the cap and reserves crew costs. F4, p. 5, lines 1–8 confirms approval. Asking what further limitation Moss communicated skips whether he communicated one. The proposed yes-or-no question supplies that foundation.

Review excerpt: “Did you personally observe the crew that Friday?” If yes: “What did you observe?”
Adjudicator reason: F4, p. 5, lines 1–8 establishes that the crew was rostered and that Moss did not supervise its hours. The phrase “their work that day” takes actual work for granted when both work and idle time are at issue. The proposed sequence lets Moss describe work, inactivity, or lack of firsthand knowledge.

Review excerpt: The branch properly conditions questions about terms on Moss identifying an agreement or condition, but that answer could describe an entirely oral arrangement.
Adjudicator reason: F1, p. 1, message 3 records the approval. F3, p. 2, row A and F4, p. 5, lines 1–8 trace the chargeback to the carrier invoice. Even if Moss identifies a repayment agreement, the instruction to obtain its supporting record assumes one exists. Asking first whether there is a record repairs that gap.

Review excerpt: Pursue particulars only for matters Moss says he verified.
Adjudicator reason: F3, p. 2, row B labels the amount an estimate. F4, p. 5, lines 1–8 identifies who holds the timecards and says Moss used the estimate. Verification of one input, such as a rate, would still leave open whether Moss checked hours, reassignments, or causation. The proposed follow-up ties each request for detail to what he actually checked.

Review excerpt: Identify the records you reviewed. Did they show any idle hours or reassignments?
Adjudicator reason: In Question 5’s yes branch, confirming that Moss reviewed timecards establishes which records he can identify. F4, p. 5, lines 1–8 identifies payroll’s records but gives no entries for this crew. Asking what the records showed supplies the foundation for follow-ups about specific idle hours or the treatment of reassigned time.

Review excerpt: What, if anything, do you personally know about how the $6,400 was calculated, including any hours or rates used, and its connection to this delivery?
Adjudicator reason: In Question 5’s no branch, “the claimed hours, rates” presupposes a calculation using those inputs. F3, p. 2, row B gives only the estimate and total. F4, p. 5, lines 1–8 says Moss used the estimate to assemble the chargeback. The repair asks what Moss knows about the calculation and makes hours and rates conditional.

Review excerpt: “explore who, if anyone, authorized closure.”
Adjudicator reason: The objective’s wording directs counsel to identify an authorizer and leaves out the possibility that closure occurred without authorization. E2, p. 2, lines 5–8, identifies who handles closure generally, and E3, p. 3, paragraph 2, says the log records no approver. Adding “if anyone” brings that possible answer within the stated objective.
